elements.texte:
[cheerful] We start with the coaches table.

We write CREATE TABLE, the table name, then its columns in parentheses, separated by commas.

Each column has a name, followed by its type: the kind of values it holds.

Integer for a whole number, real for a decimal number, text for text.

A column can also have a constraint: a rule its values must follow.

Your turn!

Primary key makes ID the primary key of the table: unique, and never empty.

A coach always has a first name and a last name: not null makes them required.

Two coaches can’t have the same email address: UNIQUE forbids duplicates.

The database will reject any row that breaks these constraints.

elements.texte:
[cheerful] Last, the cards table, for the membership cards.

Like coach underscore ID, customer underscore ID is required: a card always has an owner.

DEFAULT gives the column a value when none is given.

CHECK is a constraint that checks a condition on each value.

Your turn!

With DEFAULT 10, a card created with no balance given gets 10 sessions.

We write CHECK (sessions greater than or equal to 0): the balance can drop to 0, but not below.
